newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs trade steady-up $0.50-trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs trade steady-up $0.50-trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hogs traded steady to $0.50 per cwt higher in reaction to sharply higher cash pork prices Friday and light receipts at several Midwest markets Monday, livestock dealers said.

Interior Iowa sources reported steady trades at $54.00 at country points and $55.50 at packing plants. Dealers said Friday's $56.00 top was on a few hogs, and could be reached Monday as well. Illinois sources reported $0.50 higher trades at $52.50 to $54.50 at packing plants.
Indiana reported steady trades with tops at $53.00 in the country and $54.00 delivered to packing plants.
The $54.25 paid Friday in Indiana was an extreme top, but could be tested later Monday, dealers there said. Ohio reported $0.50 higher trades with $52.50 tops at country plants.
Despite sharply higher cash pork prices Friday, livestock dealers said tight hog supplies have meat packers scaling back slaughter.
For instance, IBP Inc on Thursday last week announced it made "significant" cutbacks in production at its seven pork plants last week and this week.
USDA reported cash pork cutout values rose $1.71 to $1.54 per cwt Friday.
In Iowa, hog shipments were impeded by icy country roads after last week's storm. Also, electrical power, knocked out by the storm, has yet to be restored to some rural areas.
